memory_update.text: SYF should be retained as the reference benchmark for scaled private-label, promotional-financing, credit/fraud decisioning, and merchant-partner integration in the consumer-credit enablement node.

BFH is the cleanest underfollowed direct candidate above $1B market cap: private-label/co-brand lender plus Bread Pay installment/split-pay rails, but survival through later layers depends on credit-quality and partner-renewal evidence.

PGY belongs in the underfollowed lane as a balance-sheet-lighter AI underwriting/capital-network candidate with POS partner exposure; later layers must verify vertical mix, partner concentration, capital-market demand, and true-lender risk.

KPLT is a speculative_shadow micro-cap exception with direct non-prime POS lease-to-own exposure; do not promote without confirming post-merger status, merchant concentration, originations quality, and liquidity.

For this node, direct exposure is not automatically positive: the same underwriting, servicing, and merchant-financing rails can become risk concentrators when delinquencies, funding costs, regulatory scrutiny, or retailer concentration rise.

Next pass should search adjacent software/data/fraud names such as credit bureaus, identity-verification providers, ecommerce fraud platforms, and card-processing/merchant-acquiring rails, because this pass focused on direct public lenders/POS financing platforms.
Synchrony is the reference benchmark for the node, but should not dominate the underfollowed lane because it is a scaled, well-known consumer-finance platform.
Bread Financial is a smaller private-label/co-brand credit-card servicer with direct consumer-discretionary category exposure and material need to verify partner concentration and credit-cycle risk.

Riskified is a balance-sheet-light fraud and chargeback-risk supplier that may be a cleaner chokepoint exposure than lenders if ecommerce merchants need higher checkout approval rates without absorbing fraud losses.
Pagaya belongs in speculative_shadow: the AI underwriting and funding rail is directly relevant, but the thesis can fail quickly if consumer-credit losses or securitization funding conditions worsen.
Layer 2 should add hard market-cap, analyst-coverage, valuation, and ownership checks; this Layer 1B pass intentionally avoids buy/sell conclusions and target prices.
SYF should be retained as the reference benchmark for private-label and co-brand card economics, but not treated as the main underfollowed discovery target.
BFH is an underfollowed mid-cap candidate for retailer credit infrastructure; survival in later layers depends on credit quality, partner retention, and Bread Pay traction.
PRG is a small-cap checkout-financing candidate with unusually direct POS relevance; key later-layer risk is POS partner concentration and lease/write-off performance in a weak consumer environment.
RSKD is a balance-sheet-light fraud and chargeback gate candidate; it may fit the preferred chokepoint angle better than lenders if merchant approval-rate and chargeback economics are improving.

Need a later pass on merchant acquirers and embedded-payment processors such as PRTH, FOUR, and lower-cap vertical payment names to map merchant-financing rails separately from consumer-credit underwriting.

The node splits into two risk regimes: software/data fraud infrastructure can benefit from higher ecommerce risk without taking credit losses, while lenders/lease-to-own providers can benefit from credit demand but absorb delinquencies, funding-cost pressure, and regulatory risk.
Add SYF as the reference benchmark for scaled private-label/co-brand consumer-credit rails; use it to compare smaller lenders and software/data processors rather than as the main alpha target.
Add BFH to the underfollowed lane as a mid-cap private-label/co-brand card issuer with strong retailer-conversion relevance but material partner concentration and credit-cycle risk.
Add RSKD as a balance-sheet-light ecommerce fraud and conversion-control candidate adjacent to consumer-credit enablement; evidence burden is merchant ROI, retention, and vertical GMV exposure.

Add PGY as speculative_shadow: potentially embedded AI underwriting infrastructure for consumer-credit approvals, but later layers must verify off-balance-sheet economics, securitization dependence, and credit-quality exposure.

PROG Holdings, Atlanticus, Katapult, Sezzle, LendingClub, Upstart, FICO, and merchant-acquiring/payment processors remain relevant adjacent names but were not included due to the four-candidate cap; next pass should separate lender risk from software/data and POS lease-to-own exposure.
